semantic_correction.stem: An asymptomatic, average-risk 47-year-old adult asks whether colorectal cancer screening can wait until age 50. Which response best reflects the current USPSTF recommendation?

options.A: Screening should begin now; the USPSTF recommends colorectal cancer screening for average-risk adults ages 45 to 49.
options.B: Screening can wait until age 50 because adults ages 45 to 49 are not included in the current USPSTF recommendation.
options.C: Screening is generally deferred until age 76 unless symptoms or a high-risk hereditary condition develop earlier.
options.D: Screening before age 50 is based on family history rather than age, so an average-risk 47-year-old should wait.

semantic_correction.rationale: The current USPSTF recommendation states that adults ages 45 to 49 should be screened for colorectal cancer (Grade B) and adults ages 50 to 75 should be screened (Grade A). The recommendation applies to adults age 45 years and older who do not have signs or symptoms of colorectal cancer and are at average risk. Therefore an asymptomatic, average-risk 47-year-old is within the recommended screening population and should not wait solely until age 50.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Apply the current USPSTF recommendation to begin colorectal cancer screening at age 45 for asymptomatic adults at average risk.

semantic_correction.correction_summary_append: RULE1 cleanup: removed 'only' distractor cueing, simplified the correct answer, and anchored the age-45 threshold to the current USPSTF Grade B recommendation for asymptomatic average-risk adults ages 45 to 49.

audit_findings_append.finding: The revised item tests the current age-45 screening threshold without family-history or symptom-based distractor ambiguity.

option_audit.A: Correct. USPSTF recommends screening adults ages 45 to 49 and applies this to asymptomatic adults at average risk.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. Adults ages 45 to 49 are explicitly included in the current recommendation.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. Age 76 is the beginning of the selectively-offered screening range, not the starting age for routine screening.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. Average-risk age alone supports screening beginning at 45 under the current USPSTF recommendation.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. A alone correctly applies the current USPSTF age and risk criteria to this 47-year-old.
cueing_check: All four options are screening-timing statements of comparable length and specificity; no absolute-word or unique-length cue identifies A.
